title: Windowed Momentum Scoring (WMS) — balancing short-term SLA pressure with long-term platform bets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Propose and pilot 'Windowed Momentum Scoring' (WMS), a prioritization heuristic that extends RICE by adding (1) a temporal momentum factor capturing recent signal changes, (2) a capacity-aware cost multiplier (tokens and Dedicated capacity pressure), and (3) an explicit latency-penalty term for SLA-sensitive initiatives. Goal is to improve selection of initiatives across short-cycle tactical work (SLO fixes, incident follow-ups) and longer-term platform bets (runtime kernel selection, quantization recommendations) so planning reflects both business velocity and operational constraints.

Why: Existing RICE-only scores underweight near-term operational risk and capacity constraints that materially change unit economics. Several recent incidents and Dedicated capacity planning conversations showed we need a way to surface work that is small effort but high short-term risk, and to de-prioritize high-effort projects when token-economics or latency tail risk would negate value. WMS keeps RICE's simplicity while encoding those operational multipliers.

Core idea / verbal formula: Score = (Reach * Impact * Momentum) / (Effort * CostMultiplier * (1 + LatencyPenalty))
- Reach, Impact, Effort: measured as in RICE (numeric estimates).
- Momentum: a multiplicative factor >0 that reflects short-term change in signals (examples below). Momentum is windowed over recent cycles (default 4 weeks) and uses exponential decay so fresh signals matter more. Momentum >1 boosts initiatives gaining traction or showing escalating risk; <1 downweights stale opportunities.
- CostMultiplier: derived from token-economics forecast and Dedicated capacity pressure; >1 if expected unit cost rises or capacity contention likely. We compute a normalized multiplier combining forecasted cost-per-token delta and a capacity scarcity index.
- LatencyPenalty: maps expected 95th Pctl latency delta (if rollout) to a bounded penalty in [0, 2]; steep above SLA thresholds. This avoids choosing projects that materially worsen tail latency without commensurate value.

Implementation notes:
1) Momentum signals (examples): weekly active request delta, regression counts in quality monitoring, new customer requests flagged as high-risk, and adoption slope from A/B experiments. Each signal is normalized, combined with weights, then exponentiated into a single multiplicative Momentum term.
2) CostMultiplier computation: combine forecasted delta in $/1M tokens (7-day moving average vs baseline) and Dedicated capacity utilization delta over 30d. Normalize both to 0.5..2.0 and multiply.
3) LatencyPenalty mapping: logistic function with knee at SLA threshold (e.g., 200ms p95) so small deltas produce small penalties and large regressions produce heavy penalties.
4) Governance: PMs set default weights for Momentum and Cost signals per product area; engineering may override for infra-only projects after review.

Pilot plan: apply WMS to next two quarterly cycles for a subset of initiatives (Platform, Runtime, Console). Run side-by-side scoring with existing RICE for 8 weeks and track changes in selected initiatives, realized token-econ delta, and SLA regressions. Evaluate lift in OKR attainment and incident counts.

Deliverables:
- Scoring spec doc (Confluence) with formulas and normalization ranges.
- Spreadsheet + script to compute WMS for candidate initiatives from our planning intake.
- Example scoring applied to current backlog (10 initiatives) with divergence analysis vs RICE.
- Console UI mock for PMs to see Momentum breakdown per initiative.

Risks/Tradeoffs:
- More signals increases complexity and calibration effort; risk of subjective weight tuning. Mitigate by keeping default weights conservative and requiring data-backed overrides.
- Momentum may over-prioritize noisy short-lived spikes; use exponential decay and require minimum sustained signal to reach Momentum >1.5.

Recommended initial normalization ranges: Reach [0.1..10], Impact [0.2..8], Effort [1..40], Momentum [0.5..3], CostMultiplier [0.6..2], LatencyPenalty [0..2]. These ranges will be tuned in the pilot.

Notes on uniqueness: WMS is intentionally windowed and capacity-aware; unlike plain RICE it integrates token-econ forecasts and a latency tail penalty to make tradeoffs explicit for inference workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence spec published describing Momentum signals, normalization, and example calculations
Script (Python/SQL) that computes WMS for a batch of initiatives using existing planning fields and monitoring signals
Pilot dataset produced comparing WMS vs RICE on 10-15 initiatives with a short writeup of divergences and recommended changes
Stakeholder review completed with Eng Leads, Platform PMs, and Solutions (approval recorded in comments)
